ROBUST

The ROBUST project involves a long-term trial of electric shared mobility hubs in four urban locations in Ireland, namely Dublin, Waterford, Galway and Letterkenny. The installed hub infrastructure initially comprises e-car charge points, electric cars, e-bikes and e-cargo bikes (provided by partners ESB & Enterprise). This is expected to be further expanded or otherwise altered to offer further micro-mobility options during the trial. The two-year trial will provide an opportunity to study the persistence of modal shift and, through the trial, the building of national capacity to expand the understanding around mobility hubs and apply it country-wide.

Mobility hubs show evidence of being an effective intervention to change travel behaviours, and the ROBUST project seeks to develop an evidence-informed toolkit for their deployment. This toolkit will provide guidance and support to policymakers and test transport policy scenarios that could facilitate the implementation of this solution. The project also aims to serve as an incubator, accelerating the uptake of electric mobility options by allowing interacting with future mobility technologies and removing barriers through participatory research. Various stakeholders will be engaged during the trial in the process of hub evolution through stakeholder and co-creation workshops.

The ROBUST project uses an experimental design comparing prior-to-trial travel behaviour, engagement with the hub modal options and after-trial persistence of the modal shift. This project is the first for Ireland in that it will trial this new mobility option in our largest city, a regional city, a regional hub and in a less populated context. Outcomes from the project will provide evidence of how these options operate in different contexts.

ROBUST has been funded by the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland under the SEAI Research, Development & Demonstration Funding Programme 2022 (grant number 22/RDD/840) and is being led by Trinity College Dublin (TCD). Partners and collaborators in ROBUST also include researchers, practitioners and others from: Atlantic Technological University (ATU); ESB Group; Enterprise Holdings UK and Ireland; MOBY; Donegal County Council; Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council; Galway County Council; Galway City Council; Letterkenny Milford Municipal District; the Northern & Western Assembly; Waterford City and County

Focus groups and Co-design workshops

The hubs will serve as an incubator, accelerating the uptake of electric mobility options by allowing interacting with future mobility technologies and removing barriers through participatory research. Various stakeholders will be engaged in the process of hub evolution through stakeholder workshops and co-creation workshops. The workshops with various groups of stakeholders will be used for relationships building, knowledge exchange and evaluation of progress and its direction. The co-creation workshops will be organized multiple times during the trial to involve actors in the development of the hubs; where main focus will be placed on frequent hub users to involve them in the recruitment process of trial participants and empower them to become the leaders of bottom-up initiatives. The knowledge obtain from multi-actor participation will then be translated into tangible solutions for hub implementation and disseminated in the form of toolkits for policymakers and booklets for communities giving insights into the impact of travel behaviour change.

Toolkit for replicating hubs, and a tooolbox for policymakers:

The toolkit for replicating hubs will define the criteria for successful implementation of shared-mobility networks and will be a result of multidisciplinary work. The first generation of shared mobility solutions has proven to be attractive to users so far. However, the lack of sufficient expertise, guidelines and tools available for adequate design and standard resulted in cancelled projects, compromised safety and reduced life cycle of vehicles (Frank et al., 2021).

The toolbox for transport trial appraisal will be developed to allow policymakers to evaluate innovative solutions and benchmark their performance. The toolbox would update the recent appraisal document used by the Department of Transport by incorporating the newest development in the transport field.
